newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - BHP rated a "sell".
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - BHP rated a "sell".

text.p: Australian brokerage Macquarie Equities has recommended clients sell shares in The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), arguing the nation's biggest company has failed to maximise returns and will continue to underperform.

The brokerage said in a report to clients this month it expected the resources group to report a flat net profit before abnormals of A$1.28 billion for the year to May 31, 1997, compared with A$1.29 billion in 1995/96.
It forecast profit to grow to A$1.37 billion in 1997/98, but did not expect BHP's strong 1994/95 profit of A$1.6 billion to be matched until 1998/99.
BHP's record earnings per share (EPS) of 104.7 cents are unlikely to be exceeded before the end of the decade, it added.
"BHP should be sold because it will continue to underperform," said the report, by analyst Greg Yeatman.
The report did not see copper and steel prices returning in the near term to levels that underpinned the record 1994/95 EPS but said BHP's long-term task was to maximise return on assets.
"The evidence is compelling," the report said. "Just under one-third of total assets provide two-thirds of operating profit. Over two-third of total assets are underperforming."

BHP possesses "daunting" underlying strength, the report said, citing its share of Bass Strait oil fields, of the La Escondida copper mine in Chile and of the North West Shelf gas fields, as well as BHP's iron ore, coal and steel assets.
"The message of this report belies the (sell) recommendation...," the report said.
"The long-term challenge is to extract qualitatively better returns from the balance of its assets," it added.
The underperforming segment of BHP's balance sheet has grown by A$10.5 billion over the past six years to A$24.2 billion in 1995/96, the report said.
"BHP recognises the need to change, and has initiated change. More needs to be done," it said.
"BHP needs to fully communicate the minimum financial performance benchmarks required of its assets anbd businesses."
The brokerage suggested BHP's steel division, which recently announced a major review of costs, should provide a detailed statement of the review's financial objectives.
BHP Steel has said it aims to slash hundreds of millions of dollars from its cost base but has not divulged its target.
BHP shares have been hammered in recent months due to weak copper prices and a prolonged slump in steel markets.
The stock was trading at A$16.75 at 0400 GMT on Thursday, off its low for the year so far of A$15.58 but well down on its year high of A$20.05.
